vulnerabilities.description: A heap-based buffer overflow flaw was found in Cyrus SASL. The add_to_challenge() function in the DIGEST-MD5 plugin computes the size of the buffer needed for a challenge/response field before DIGEST-MD5 quoting is applied, but does not recompute that size when quoting (escaping special characters) makes the value longer. The under-sized buffer is then passed to strcat(), causing a heap-based out-of-bounds write whose size depends on attacker-controlled input. A malicious or on-path DIGEST-MD5 (or HTTP Digest) server can trigger this flaw in a connecting client by supplying a crafted challenge field, such as realm or nonce, most likely resulting in a crash of the client application.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. The vulnerable DIGEST-MD5 plugin is not installed in the image.

ratings.justification: CNA score; NVD had not yet published its own score at assessment time.
The DIGEST-MD5 plugin that contains the flaw is not installed in the image.

analysis.detail: The heap buffer overflow is in add_to_challenge() in the Cyrus SASL DIGEST-MD5 plugin. The liquibase/liquibase-secure 6.0.3 image installs only the SASL library and the sasldb plugin package; the DIGEST-MD5 plugin (shipped in the separate libsasl2-modules package) is not installed, so the vulnerable code is not present. Liquibase itself does not use Cyrus SASL. Ubuntu has deferred the issue pending an upstream fix.
